answer: At dawn a Sybil farm spins up fake agents, but every identity must first mine an admission proof: grab a single-use challenge and find a nonce whose SHA-256 has enough leading zero bits. Proofs expire and are spent once, and the required bits climb whenever join traffic surges. Growing an orchard of hundreds of fakes means paying that compute per head, while a comet burst of registrations only makes each extra identity cost about twice the last.
